sn19.10:1.1: The “gnomes” (_kumbhaṇḍa_, Sanskrit _kuṣmāṇḍa_, “pumpkin-belly”) were a race of lesser deities often depicted as pot-bellied, ugly and misshapen, though reckoned as subjects of the four great kings ([dn20:9.13]()). _Kumbha_ also means “pot” and _aṇḍa_ “testicle” ([mn56:25.4]()). Compare the fiendish _kumbhamuṣka_ (“pot-scrotum”) of Atharva Veda 8.6.15, 11.9.17. Perhaps conflated with _kuṣumbha_, an insect’s venom-sack (Atharva Veda 2.32.6).
sn19.10:1.2: While the humorously painful imagery here is clear, it is less clear that the literal sense “pot-balls” was meant in general for the _kumbhaṇḍa_ as a deity. Here it is used adjectivally of a man.
sn19.10:1.6: A _gāmakūṭa_ is a “village head” , so _kūṭa_ here means “summit” rather than its other sense of “fraud”, though the senses might be conflated. The commentary explains it as “an official who makes judgements”. The suffix _-ka_ in the form here (_gāmakūṭaka_) must have its belittling sense like _muṇḍakā samaṇakā_ (“shavelings, fake ascetics”). Kauṭilya depicts the _grāmakūṭa_ as acting on the whispers of an informant (Arthaśāstra 4.4.9). Perhaps his testicles are the size of the pots of gold he made through extortion and blackmail.
